title: session-eviction-ttl-reclaim-and-cancel-safepoints-openai-compat
author: Leah Kim
description: Motivation: production streaming sessions occasionally become orphaned when clients disconnect without sending a cancel, leading to KV-cache leaks and inflated resource use. Additionally, OpenAI-compatible clients expect a predictable cancel semantics (immediate cancel + short resume window) which our existing session lifecycle did not guarantee under high load. This PR introduces (1) an eviction + reclaim TTL for idle/inactive sessions with a safe reclaim window and soft-cancel markers, (2) a client-side 'soft-cancel' window to allow reconnect+resume semantics compatible with OpenAI-style cancellations, and (3) a compatibility shim so function/tool-calling idempotency and structured-output flushes behave consistently during cancel/reclaim races. Design summary: - Session reclaim model: sessions are now tracked with two timeouts: idle_eviction_ms (short eviction signal used for routing decisions) and reclaim_ttl_ms (how long the session KV/cache is kept for potential resume). Evicted sessions move to 'reclaimable' state and are eligible for GC after reclaim_ttl_ms. - Soft-cancel safepoints: on receiving a client cancel, we mark the stream with a soft-cancel safepoint (soft_cancel_ts) and propagate a cancellable token to downstream toolcall execution. The server will still complete short-lived downstream calls within soft_cancel_window_ms before hard abort, enabling idempotent toolcalls and structured-output flushes. - Reconnect/resume behavior: clients that reconnect within reclaim_ttl_ms can reattach and continue if the server has not reclaimed the session; the API includes a new header X-Session-Reattach: <session-id> to attach. The OpenAI compatibility layer will translate openai-cancel into a soft-cancel followed by an expire timeline that matches expected behavior for existing clients. - Backpressure and fallback: if reclaim queues grow, an eviction prioritizer drops oldest reclaimable sessions first; we expose metrics to SRE to tune policies. - Safety & idempotency: function calls initiated before soft-cancel are annotated with a call_id and a finalizer hook; if reclaimed while a call is in-flight, the runtime will prefer replay semantics over duplicate execution when call_id is present. Files changed are intentionally concise: session lifecycle state machine, eviction queue implementation, header parsing in openai-adapter, and unit+integration tests. Rollout & feature flags: session.reclaim_ttl_ms and session.soft_cancel_window_ms are controlled by flags; default values are conservative (reclaim_ttl=5m, soft_cancel=3s) and will be ramped via canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Migration notes: operators should be aware of new memory metrics (session_reclaim_count, session_active_reclaimable) and may want to lower reclaim_ttl for low-memory clusters. Test plan: unit tests for state transitions, deterministic integration tests simulating disconnect + reconnect races, e2e with openai-adapter exercising toolcall idempotency and structured-output flush semantics. CI: full test-suite + a new stress job (streaming-orphan-stress) added to the pipeline. See linked linear items for performance targets and further instrumentation tasks.

release_notes: Adds session reclaim TTL and soft-cancel safepoints to improve streaming stability and OpenAI compatibility. Introduces session.reclaim_ttl_ms and session.soft_cancel_window_ms feature flags, X-Session-Reattach header for reconnect/resume, and idempotency markers for function/tool calls to avoid duplicate side-effects during reclaim races. Metrics: session_reclaim_count, session_active_reclaimable.
